title: The Gospel of Matthew Timeline
sub: Five Discourses · Matthew's Own Architecture · Every Chapter, Chapter & Verse
desc: The longest Gospel, built around five major blocks of Jesus' own teaching — the Sermon on the Mount, the Mission Discourse, the Parables of the Kingdom, the Church Discourse, and the Olivet Discourse — each closed with the same formula, 'when Jesus had finished these words.' Written for a Jewish audience, with more fulfilled-prophecy citations than any other Gospel. Entries marked ✔Mt note material found nowhere else in the Gospels.

eras.label: Era One · Matthew 1:1-2:23
eras.name: Genealogy and Infancy
eras.dates: A king-shaped birth story, told entirely from Joseph's side

events.title: The Genealogy: Abraham to David to the Christ
events.detail: Matthew opens with a formal record, not a story — forty-two generations arranged in three neat sets of fourteen, tracing Jesus back through David to Abraham. The shape is the argument: this Gospel's very first sentence stakes Jesus' claim to Israel's messianic and patriarchal promises before a single scene has happened.

events.title: Joseph's Dream; 'Immanuel'
events.detail: Unlike Luke, Matthew tells the whole nativity through Joseph, not Mary — an angel visits him in a dream, not her, to explain the pregnancy and assign the name Jesus. Matthew's own aside translates Isaiah's sign-child, Immanuel, as 'God with us,' a title this Gospel will return to at its very last verse.

events.title: The Magi and the Star
events.detail: Found only in Matthew: foreign astrologers, not shepherds, follow a star to Bethlehem and bring gold, frankincense, and myrrh — while Herod, threatened, quietly plots. The magi's gifts and their refusal to report back to Herod set up everything that follows in this chapter.

events.title: Flight to Egypt; the Slaughter of the Innocents
events.detail: Also unique to Matthew: Herod's massacre of Bethlehem's infant boys, and the family's escape to Egypt and eventual return — each step marked by its own fulfilled prophecy (Hosea's 'out of Egypt I called my son,' Jeremiah's Rachel weeping for her children). No other Gospel records this material at all.

eras.label: Era Two · Matthew 3:1-4:25
eras.name: Preparation for Ministry
eras.dates: Wilderness, river, wilderness again, then the work begins

events.title: John the Baptist Prepares the Way
events.detail: John appears already quoting Isaiah's 'voice crying in the wilderness,' and turns on the Pharisees and Sadducees who come to him with real venom — 'you brood of vipers' — warning that ancestry from Abraham means nothing without real fruit.

events.title: The Baptism of Jesus
events.detail: John tries to refuse, insisting Jesus should baptize him instead; Jesus overrules him — 'to fulfill all righteousness' — and the heavens open with the same voice and dove that mark every Synoptic account of this moment: 'This is My beloved Son.'

events.title: The Temptation in the Wilderness
events.detail: Forty days of fasting, then three tests, each answered from Deuteronomy — bread, a leap from the temple, and the kingdoms of the world offered outright. The devil even misquotes Scripture back at Jesus, and Jesus corrects the misquote with more Scripture rather than argument.

events.title: Ministry Begins in Galilee; the First Disciples Called
events.detail: Jesus relocates to Capernaum explicitly to fulfill Isaiah's promise to 'Galilee of the Gentiles,' then calls two sets of fishermen brothers with nothing but a command — 'immediately they left their nets' — before the chapter closes with crowds already flooding in from Syria and the Decapolis.

eras.label: Era Three · Matthew 5:1-7:29
eras.name: Discourse 1 — The Sermon on the Mount
eras.dates: Matthew's first and longest block of Jesus' own teaching, delivered from a mountain

events.title: The Beatitudes; Salt and Light
events.detail: Nine blessings that invert ordinary expectation — the poor in spirit, the mourning, the persecuted, all called blessed — followed by two images of what the crowd itself is for: salt that must stay salty, a city on a hill that cannot hide.

events.title: 'You Have Heard It Said... But I Say to You'
events.detail: Jesus insists he has come to fulfill the Law, not abolish it, then repeatedly takes a familiar commandment — murder, adultery, oaths, retaliation, love of neighbor — and pushes it to its root motive, closing on the hardest line in the whole sermon: 'love your enemies.'

events.title: Giving, Prayer, and the Lord's Prayer
events.detail: Three private disciplines — almsgiving, prayer, fasting — each contrasted with hypocrites performing for an audience. At the center sits the model prayer itself, the most repeated words in Christian history, taught here as the corrective to 'meaningless repetition.'

events.title: Treasure in Heaven; Do Not Worry
events.detail: Two connected images: treasure that moths and thieves can't reach, and birds and lilies as proof that anxiety accomplishes nothing God hasn't already provided for. The chapter's famous closing line reframes worry itself as a rival god: 'you cannot serve God and wealth.'

events.title: Judging, the Golden Rule, and the Two Builders
events.detail: The sermon closes with warnings about judgment, the Golden Rule stated as the summary of 'the Law and the Prophets,' the narrow gate, and a final parable contrasting a house built on rock against one built on sand. Matthew's own closing narration marks the discourse's end with a formula this Gospel repeats four more times: 'when Jesus had finished these words, the crowds were astonished.'

eras.label: Era Four · Matthew 8:1-9:38
eras.name: Ten Miracles and a Call to Follow
eras.dates: Authority demonstrated in the same rapid, list-like style Matthew used for teaching

events.title: A Leper, a Centurion's Servant, and Peter's Mother-in-Law
events.detail: Three healings in a row, the middle one remarkable for who asks: a Roman centurion, whose logic of authority — 'I say to this man, Go, and he goes' — earns the line 'I have not found such great faith with anyone in Israel.'

events.title: The Cost of Following; Calming the Storm
events.detail: A would-be follower is told the Son of Man has 'nowhere to lay His head'; then, in the boat, Jesus asleep through a storm that terrifies seasoned fishermen wakes only to calm both the wind and their 'little faith' with the same rebuke.

events.title: Two Demoniacs; the Paralytic Let Down Through the Roof
events.detail: Across the sea in Gentile territory, demons driven into a herd of pigs; back in his 'own city,' a paralyzed man's sins forgiven before his legs are healed — the harder claim proven by the easier-to-verify one, exactly as in Mark and Luke's parallel versions of this scene.

events.title: Matthew's Own Call; Bridegroom, Wineskins
events.detail: The tax collector Matthew, presumably the Gospel's own namesake, gets called from his tax booth the same way the fishermen were — and immediately hosts a dinner full of 'tax collectors and sinners' that draws the Pharisees' complaint and Jesus' answer about a physician's real patients.

events.title: A Dead Girl, a Bleeding Woman, and Two Blind Men
events.detail: A synagogue official's dead daughter and a woman with a twelve-year hemorrhage are healed in the same interwoven scene; two blind men and a mute demoniac follow. The section closes on the line that becomes the hinge into the next discourse: 'the harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few.'

eras.label: Era Five · Matthew 10:1-11:1
eras.name: Discourse 2 — The Mission Discourse
eras.dates: Instructions for the Twelve, sent out as Jesus' own delegated authority

events.title: The Twelve Named and Sent
events.detail: All twelve apostles listed by name, Judas Iscariot marked last as the one who 'betrayed Him' even before the story requires it, then sent out with authority over disease and unclean spirits and strict instructions to travel light — no gold, no bag, no second tunic.

events.title: Persecution Foretold; 'Not Peace, but a Sword'
events.detail: The tone turns hard fast — 'sheep in the midst of wolves,' families turning on each other, a warning that following Jesus can cost everything a disciple has. Matthew closes the discourse with its own formula, verse 11:1: 'when Jesus had finished giving instructions to His twelve disciples, He departed from there.'

eras.label: Era Six · Matthew 11:2-12:50
eras.name: Questions and Growing Opposition
eras.dates: John's doubt from prison, woes on unrepentant towns, and open Sabbath conflict

events.title: John's Question from Prison
events.detail: Even John the Baptist, in prison, sends disciples to ask if Jesus is really 'the One who is to come' — Jesus answers not with a yes, but with a list of what's happening: the blind see, the dead are raised, the poor hear good news, echoing Isaiah's own messianic checklist.

events.title: Woes on Unrepentant Cities; 'Come to Me, All Who Are Weary'
events.detail: Chorazin, Bethsaida, and Capernaum are denounced by name for witnessing miracles and not repenting — immediately followed by the gentlest invitation in the whole Gospel, 'my yoke is easy and my burden is light,' the same voice capable of both judgment and comfort in one breath.

events.title: Sabbath Controversies; 'Lord of the Sabbath'
events.detail: Grainfields and a withered hand, both on the Sabbath, both defended by appeal to David and to mercy over sacrifice — and both ending with the Pharisees plotting to destroy him, a plot Matthew frames with a long quotation from Isaiah's 'Servant' poem.

events.title: The Beelzebul Charge; True Family
events.detail: Accused of casting out demons by Satan's own power, Jesus answers with the simple logic of a divided kingdom, then warns of the one sin that 'shall not be forgiven' — before closing, as in Mark, by redefining family itself around 'whoever does the will of My Father.'

eras.label: Era Seven · Matthew 13:1-53
eras.name: Discourse 3 — Parables of the Kingdom
eras.dates: Seven parables in one sitting, told from a boat to a crowd on the beach

events.title: The Sower, Explained in Private
events.detail: The same public-story-private-explanation pattern as Mark: seed on four kinds of ground, told to the whole crowd, then unpacked verse by verse only once the disciples ask — 'to you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom.'

events.title: Wheat and Tares, Mustard Seed, Leaven — Explained
events.detail: Matthew alone preserves the wheat-and-tares parable and its full private explanation — the enemy who sows weeds among good grain is the devil, the harvest is the end of the age — alongside the shorter mustard-seed and leaven parables shared with the other Synoptics.

events.title: Hidden Treasure, a Pearl, a Dragnet
events.detail: Three final short parables about a kingdom worth abandoning everything else for — a treasure, a pearl, a net that sorts good fish from bad — closing on the discourse formula again: 'when Jesus had finished these parables, He departed from there.'

eras.label: Era Eight · Matthew 13:54-16:20
eras.name: Rejection to Confession
eras.dates: From a hometown that won't believe him to a disciple who finally does

events.title: Rejection at Nazareth
events.detail: 'Is not this the carpenter's son?' His own hometown takes offense at him, and Matthew records the same honest admission as Mark: 'He did not do many miracles there because of their unbelief.'

events.title: The Death of John the Baptist
events.detail: Herod's birthday oath, Herodias's daughter's dance, and a head delivered on a platter — the same grim account as Mark's, ending simply: John's disciples 'buried it, and they went and reported to Jesus.'

events.title: Feeding the Five Thousand
events.detail: Five loaves and two fish stretch to feed a whole crowd with twelve baskets left over — the one miracle every Gospel records, here framed as Jesus' response to hearing about John's death.

events.title: Walking on Water; Peter Steps Out
events.detail: Unique to Matthew: Peter asks to walk out on the water too, manages several steps, then sinks the moment he notices the wind — 'you of little faith, why did you doubt?' — a scene found in no other Gospel.

events.title: Tradition of the Elders; What Truly Defiles
events.detail: Pharisees challenge unwashed hands; Jesus counters with the Corban loophole that lets people dodge caring for their own parents, then teaches the crowd that defilement comes from the heart, not the stomach.

events.title: The Canaanite Woman's Faith
events.detail: A Gentile mother's sharp comeback — 'even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their masters' table' — turns Jesus' own hard saying back on him and earns her daughter's healing along with some of the highest praise given to anyone in this Gospel: 'your faith is great.'

events.title: Feeding the Four Thousand
events.detail: A second, structurally near-identical feeding miracle — seven loaves this time, seven baskets left over — for a crowd that had 'remained with Me now three days.'

events.title: The Leaven of the Pharisees; Peter's Confession
events.detail: Pharisees and Sadducees demand a sign and get only 'the sign of Jonah'; then, at Caesarea Philippi, Peter answers the question this whole Gospel has been building toward — 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God' — and receives, uniquely in Matthew, the promise of the keys of the kingdom and the church built on 'this rock.'

eras.label: Era Nine · Matthew 16:21-17:27
eras.name: First Predictions and the Mountain
eras.dates: The turn toward Jerusalem begins, framed by a vision only three disciples see

events.title: The First Passion Prediction; 'Take Up His Cross'
events.detail: Immediately after Peter's confession, Jesus states plainly that he must suffer and die in Jerusalem — and Peter, the same disciple just praised, gets the sharpest rebuke in the Gospel for objecting: 'Get behind Me, Satan.'

events.title: The Transfiguration
events.detail: Six days later, on a mountain, Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James and John — Moses and Elijah appear, and the same voice heard at the baptism repeats itself: 'listen to Him.' Coming down, the disciples finally understand a piece of Jesus' earlier riddle: Elijah 'already came' in John the Baptist.

events.title: A Boy Healed; the Coin in the Fish's Mouth
events.detail: The disciples fail to heal a boy with seizures where Jesus succeeds ('because of your little faith'), and the chapter closes with a detail found nowhere else in the Gospels: rather than offend the temple tax collectors, Jesus tells Peter to catch a fish that will have the exact coin needed inside its mouth.

eras.label: Era Ten · Matthew 18:1-35
eras.name: Discourse 4 — The Church Discourse
eras.dates: How a community of disciples treats its own weakest and most wounded members

events.title: Becoming Like a Child; the Lost Sheep
events.detail: Asked who's greatest in the kingdom, Jesus sets a child in the middle of the group as the answer, follows it with the harshest warnings in the Gospel about causing 'little ones' to stumble, and softens back into the parable of a shepherd leaving ninety-nine sheep to find the one that wandered.

events.title: Church Discipline; the Unforgiving Servant
events.detail: A three-step process for confronting sin within the community, a promise about two or three gathered in Jesus' name, and — when Peter asks how many times to forgive — the parable of a servant forgiven an impossible debt who then chokes a fellow servant over a trivial one. The discourse closes on Matthew's formula once more: 'when Jesus had finished these words, He departed from Galilee.'

eras.label: Era Eleven · Matthew 19:1-20:34
eras.name: The Road to Jerusalem
eras.dates: Hard teachings and reversed expectations, all the way south to Jericho

events.title: Divorce; Let the Children Come
events.detail: Pharisees test Jesus on divorce; he goes back past Moses' concession to Genesis itself — 'what God has joined together, let no man separate' — then, in the next breath, welcomes the children the disciples try to turn away.

events.title: The Rich Young Man; 'With God All Things Are Possible'
events.detail: A man who has kept every commandment since youth walks away grieving rather than sell his possessions, prompting the camel-and-needle saying and Peter's own question — 'what then will there be for us?' — answered with promises of a hundredfold return and thrones for the Twelve.

events.title: The Laborers in the Vineyard
events.detail: Unique to Matthew: workers hired at different hours of the day all receive the same wage, and the landowner's answer to the grumbling of those hired first — 'is your eye envious because I am generous?' — makes the parable's point about grace rather than fairness explicit.

events.title: The Third Passion Prediction; James and John; Two Blind Men
events.detail: The most detailed of the three predictions yet, immediately undercut by a mother's request that her sons James and John get the seats of honor — Jesus redefines greatness as service one more time — before two blind beggars at Jericho, unlike the rich young man, actually follow him once healed.

eras.label: Era Twelve · Matthew 21:1-22:46
eras.name: Jerusalem Confrontation
eras.dates: One week, a cursed fig tree, and a string of public traps that all fail

events.title: The Triumphal Entry
events.detail: Matthew, characteristically, cites the prophecy behind the scene directly — Zechariah's king 'lowly, and mounted on a donkey' — and even has Jesus riding both a donkey and its colt at once, a detail read either as a doubled fulfillment or a literalistic misreading of Hebrew poetic parallelism.

events.title: Cleansing the Temple; the Cursed Fig Tree
events.detail: Money-changers driven out, quoting Isaiah and Jeremiah together; then a fig tree cursed for having no fruit withers 'at once' rather than overnight as in Mark's version — Matthew compresses the sandwich structure into a single fast scene.

events.title: 'By What Authority?'; Two Sons, the Wicked Tenants
events.detail: Chief priests demand Jesus' credentials and get trapped by his counter-question about John's baptism; two parables follow — a son who says no but obeys, and tenants who kill the vineyard owner's son — both aimed, and understood, as attacks on the religious leaders themselves.

events.title: The Wedding Feast
events.detail: A king's wedding invitation refused, then reissued to 'the main highways' — and a guest thrown out for showing up without wedding clothes, a detail unique to Matthew's version of this parable, closing on the line 'many are called, but few are chosen.'

events.title: Caesar's Coin, the Sadducees, the Greatest Commandment
events.detail: Three traps in a row — taxes to Caesar, a riddle about resurrection and remarriage, and 'which is the greatest commandment' — all defused, before Jesus poses his own unanswerable question about how the Christ can be both David's son and David's Lord. 'No one was able to answer Him a word.'

eras.label: Era Thirteen · Matthew 23:1-39
eras.name: Woes on the Pharisees
eras.dates: Jesus' last public words in the temple, and the longest single denunciation in any Gospel

events.title: 'They Do Not Practice What They Preach'
events.detail: Jesus tells the crowd to obey what the scribes and Pharisees teach but not to imitate their behavior — broadened phylacteries, the best seats, the title 'Rabbi' — before flipping the whole social order: 'whoever exalts himself shall be humbled.'

events.title: Seven Woes; 'Jerusalem, Jerusalem'
events.detail: Seven consecutive 'woe to you' denunciations — blind guides, whitewashed tombs, strained gnats and swallowed camels — give way, without warning, to grief: 'how often I wanted to gather your children together, the way a hen gathers her chicks... and you did not want it.'

eras.label: Era Fourteen · Matthew 24:1-25:46
eras.name: Discourse 5 — The Olivet Discourse
eras.dates: Matthew's longest and final teaching block, on the end of the age and how to be ready for it

events.title: Signs of the End; the Abomination of Desolation
events.detail: Asked privately about the temple's destruction and 'the end of the age,' Jesus lists wars, famines, false messiahs, and 'the abomination of desolation' spoken of by Daniel — escalating to cosmic imagery of the Son of Man 'coming on the clouds of the sky with power and great glory.'

events.title: No One Knows the Day; the Faithful and Unfaithful Slave
events.detail: 'Of that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels... but the Father alone' — followed by Noah's flood as the model for how suddenly it will come, and a parable contrasting a slave who keeps working faithfully against one who beats his fellow slaves assuming his master is delayed.

events.title: Ten Virgins; the Talents
events.detail: Two parables unique to Matthew's version of this discourse: five prepared and five unprepared bridesmaids locked out of a wedding feast, and three servants given different sums of money, judged not by how much they started with but by what they did with it.

events.title: The Sheep and the Goats
events.detail: Found only in Matthew: a final judgment scene where nations are separated by how they treated 'the least of these' — the hungry, the stranger, the sick, the imprisoned — with the King's own verdict collapsing the distance between himself and the most vulnerable: 'you did it to Me.'

eras.label: Era Fifteen · Matthew 26:1-27:66
eras.name: The Passion
eras.dates: From an anointing in Bethany to a sealed and guarded tomb

events.title: Anointing at Bethany; Judas's Bargain
events.detail: A woman pours costly perfume on Jesus' head, defended against the disciples' complaint as an anointing 'for burial'; in the very next verse Judas goes to the chief priests and agrees to betray Jesus for thirty pieces of silver, a price Matthew will connect to Zechariah's prophecy.

events.title: The Last Supper
events.detail: Bread and cup reinterpreted as 'My body' and 'My blood of the covenant, poured out for many for forgiveness of sins' — Matthew alone adds that specific phrase, 'for forgiveness of sins,' to the cup saying.

events.title: Peter's Denial Foretold
events.detail: Jesus predicts that all the disciples will fall away and, specifically, that Peter will deny him three times before the rooster crows — Peter insists, twice, that he never will.

events.title: Gethsemane
events.detail: 'My soul is deeply grieved, to the point of death.' Three times Jesus prays alone and returns to find Peter, James and John asleep; the third time he simply says it's too late — 'the hour is at hand.'

events.title: The Arrest
events.detail: Judas's kiss as the prearranged signal; a disciple's sword cut off ends with Jesus' own rebuke — 'all those who take up the sword shall perish by the sword' — and a reminder that legions of angels are available but unused, 'so that the Scriptures would be fulfilled.'

events.title: Before Caiaphas and the Sanhedrin
events.detail: False witnesses can't agree, until the high priest puts Jesus under oath directly: 'are You the Christ, the Son of God?' Jesus' answer, combining Daniel and Psalm 110, is called blasphemy on the spot, and the council condemns him.

events.title: Peter's Threefold Denial
events.detail: Exactly as predicted: a servant girl, then bystanders, press Peter three times in the courtyard, and by the third denial he's cursing and swearing he doesn't know 'the man.' The rooster crows, Peter remembers, and 'went out and cried bitterly.'

events.title: Judas's Remorse and Death
events.detail: Unique to Matthew: Judas, seeing Jesus condemned, tries to return the silver, is refused, throws the coins into the temple, and hangs himself — the chief priests using the blood money to buy the 'Field of Blood,' a detail Matthew ties to a prophecy from Jeremiah.

events.title: Before Pilate; Barabbas Released
events.detail: Pilate's wife sends a warning dream; Pilate washes his hands of the whole affair while the crowd, stirred up by the chief priests, takes on the guilt themselves — 'His blood be on us and on our children!' — a line with a long and painful afterlife in how this Gospel was later misused.

events.title: Mocked and Crucified
events.detail: A scarlet robe, a crown of thorns, a mock scepter of reed; Simon of Cyrene presses into service to carry the cross; Jesus crucified between two robbers under a sign reading 'THIS IS JESUS THE KING OF THE JEWS,' mocked by the same crowd that had shouted Hosanna days earlier.

events.title: The Death of Jesus; the Temple Veil Torn
events.detail: Darkness for three hours, then the Aramaic cry — 'Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani,' Psalm 22's opening line — kept untranslated before Matthew glosses it. At his death the temple veil tears, the earth shakes, and, in a detail found nowhere else in any Gospel, tombs open and 'many bodies of the saints' are raised and seen in Jerusalem.

events.title: Burial; the Guard at the Tomb
events.detail: Joseph of Arimathea buries the body in his own new tomb; unique to Matthew, the chief priests then ask Pilate for a guard and a sealed stone specifically to prevent a claimed resurrection — setting up the cover story this Gospel alone bothers to rebut.

eras.label: Era Sixteen · Matthew 28:1-20
eras.name: The Resurrection
eras.dates: An earthquake, an empty tomb, a bribed cover story, and a final commission on a mountain

events.title: The Empty Tomb
events.detail: An angel 'like lightning' rolls back the stone in front of the terrified guards, and the risen Jesus himself meets the women on their way to tell the disciples — 'do not be afraid; go and report to My brothers.'

events.title: The Guards Bribed
events.detail: Found only in Matthew: the chief priests pay the guards to spread a story that the disciples stole the body while they slept — a story, Matthew notes pointedly, 'widely spread among the Jews, and is to this day,' meaning this Gospel is directly answering a rumor still circulating when it was written.

events.title: The Great Commission
events.detail: On a Galilean mountain, with 'some' still doubting even as they worship, Jesus claims 'all authority... in heaven and on earth' and sends the eleven to 'make disciples of all the nations' — closing the Gospel on the same promise its second chapter opened with: 'I am with you always, even to the end of the age.'
